title: Slotted assembly pauses and fairness reconciliation playbook
creator: Maya Rangan
description:
Summary: On 2026-02-28 we observed repeated multi-region tail-latency spikes and a correlating increase in unequal request completion rates across priority classes. Symptoms manifested as long 'assembly pauses' on continuous batching nodes where slots would stop accepting inflight requests for 200–1200 ms windows. The outage surface included elevated 95th/99th token latency for text-generation routes, an increase in client-side timeouts, and degradation of fairness guarantees for P1 customers. Immediate mitigations restored steady state but did not fully address fairness skew against lower-priority traffic.

Root cause (short): A scheduler change merged in runtime-1.20 (PR #4248) altered slot reclamation timing and affinity promotion heuristics. Under bimodal traffic (bursty low-priority background and short high-priority interactive requests) the slot assignment algorithm occasionally delayed re-arming slots after a preemption path. This created transient 'assembly pauses' where the continuous batcher’s slot map held gaps. Those gaps lengthened due to the interaction with the new affinity-promote timers and our KV cache eviction policy, amplifying tail latency and allowing high-priority flows to dominate available capacity when slots resumed, causing fairness skew.

Why this is unique/different from previous incidents: Prior batch silence incidents were primarily caused by timer wheel drift or queue coalescer deadlocks. This incident is distinct because it is a state-machine coordination bug between the slot reclamation path and affinity promotion logic that only triggers on mixed-priority, mixed-shot-length workloads with a narrow timing window introduced by the recent scheduler tweak.

Detection: Grafana alert BATCH_ASSEMBLY_PAUSE_FREQUENCY fired when pause count exceeded threshold in two regions. Customer reports and synthetic SLO-monitoring test failures (run via canary-job/gen-traffic) correlated within the same 30m window. The observability traces pointed to repeated ReclaimSlot -> PromoteAffinity -> fail-to-rearm events.

Impact: Affected ~7% of serving-slices across two regions for three 30–90 minute waves. Customer-facing effects: elevated error rates for long-running generation (streaming) and thin-but-latency-sensitive chat sessions. No data loss or security exposure.

Temporary mitigations performed during the incident:
- Rolled back the affinity-promote timing change in a targeted canary slice (runtime-1.20 -> runtime-1.20-rollback patch) which reduced pause frequency by ~85% in the canary within 12 minutes (see Grafana link).
- Increased slot rearm aggressiveness on impacted nodes (hotfix: scheduler-rearm-override) to minimize pause window.
- Applied a short-term KV cache eviction leniency to avoid thrashing when slots reappeared.

Longer-term decisions and rationale: The team voted to revert the scheduler heuristic that caused the timing window and to implement a deterministic fallback rearm path if PromoteAffinity fails to complete in X ms. We will also introduce a fairness reconciliation process that periodically reweights inflight contexts to ensure slot allocation over a moving window meets configured fairness SLOs.

acceptance_criteria: Mainline reverted or updated so that the original timing change cannot reintroduce pause windows without explicit opt-in
Fast-rearm fallback merged and validated in canary with synthetic mixed workloads showing <10ms median rearm latency and <50ms 99th rearm latency
Fairness reconciliation job in place and configured; measured fairness SLO improvement of >25% reduction in per-slice skew in post-deploy evaluation
Observability dashboards reflect per-slot lifecycle and the new PromoteAffinity metrics; alerts tuned to actionable thresholds
Runbook updated and on-call trained for assembly-pause incidents
